text:
alex_k: Nightly perf alert flagged a regression on the main rollout — p50 stable, p95 +18%, p99 +7%, and throughput down ~12% since ~03:00 UTC. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood/prod/nightly/3123456789 :alarm_clock:

ci-bot: [perf-suite/nightly] regression detected for merge commit abc1234 (PR #5678). Perf artifact: https://ci.redwood/artifacts/5678/perf-report.html

maria-r: I merged #5678 yesterday afternoon — it included a small kernel ordering change and an aggressive batching window tweak. Not expecting huge tail, but could be interacting with larger requests. cc @chen-l

chen-l: Quick FYI I did a local revert of the kernel-ordering tweak and latency returned to baseline for our stress suite. Will push a tiny repro soon.

sam_w: Profiling snapshot from the nightly run attached in the CI artifact — KV miss rate jumped for long sequences. Short paste:```
requests>512 tokens: kv_miss_rate=22% (baseline 4%)
kernel_switches increased by 3.1x
latency_p99 from 240ms -> 257ms
```Looks like more requests are being routed to kernel_B (slower path) after the selector change.

nina_ops: Paused the canary rollout on prod (console) and pinned traffic to stable. If we need to revert quickly I can cut a rollback PR and promote.

alex_k: Good catch. I'm starting a bisect between good tag v2026.02 and commit abc1234 to narrow which commit introduced the regression. Steps:```
git checkout v2026.02
git bisect start abc1234 v2026.02
# run perf-suite-nightly-smoke.sh locally on the bisect worker
```Will post results as I go.

maria-r: Also will review the batching-window change in PR 5690 — it moved the low-latency threshold to prefer micro-batches which might increase KV pressure for >512 token flows.

sam_w: CI job nightly-perf-64g flagged the same trend earlier: kernel-selector fallback rate up, prefetch hits down. Logs show many requests missing the prefix cache because batching reordered prefixes. Snippet:```
[2026-03-18T03:07:12Z] prefetch: hit=173 fail=48 (23% fail)
[2026-03-18T03:07:12Z] selector: picked=kernel_B slow_path=true
```

chen-l: If the bisect points at the kernel ordering commit I'm in favor of an immediate revert of that change. Reverting the batching tweak might be safer but could harm tail for small requests. We should decide based on the bisect.

nina_ops: Drafted a revert PR: https://git/redwood/reverts/5691 and flagged it as rollover. Assigned @maria-r and @chen-l to review. If approved, I can cut the rollback and run canary smoke tonight.

alex_k: Action items for now:
- alex_k: finish bisect and post commit id causing perf delta (ETA 20m)
- maria-r & chen-l: prepare revert/patch candidates and smoke configs
- sam_w: run focused perf job that reproduces high kv miss on a bisect worker (I can share the job config)
- nina_ops: keep canary paused and stand by for rollback

maria-r: Ack. I'll also add a quick telemetry probe to the kernel selector to record weight distribution per request so we can confirm selector shifts in prod.

chen-l: If we end up reverting, let's also include a guarded feature-flag around the ordering so we can roll forward with telemetry without full exposure.

alex_k: Bisect update: narrowed it to two commits — abc1200 (kernel ordering) and abc1234 (batching window). Reproduced perf delta when kernel ordering is present.

sam_w: Confirmed on the bisect worker: toggling kernel ordering flips the p95/p99 back and forth. Looks like selector change is the smoking gun.

nina_ops: OK preparing rollback cut. Will run canary smoke after PR merge and report back.

alex_k: Thanks everyone. If rollback goes green, we'll re-run full nightly perf-suite and keep the batching tweak behind a flag until we validate KV/cache interactions. :thumbsup:
